transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Ava Kim (Redwood SE), Jared Liu (Vela CTO), Maya Torres (Vela Lead Backend), Priya Rao (Vela Security), Ethan Park (Vela Frontend)

Summary:
Quick SDK integration walkthrough covering Redwood API & Console, Python + TypeScript quickstarts, auth patterns (API key vs SSO), environment setup, and recommended next steps for a pilot. Security questions surfaced around KMS and audit logs; SE flagged benchmarking and batching recommendations.

Topics:
- Quickstart flow (Python, TS)
- Auth: API keys, SSO, scopes, rotation, KMS
- Env setup: staging vs prod, VPC/private deployments options
- Console walkthrough: keys, routes, logs, cost view
- Optimize: batching, caching, quantization suggestions

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Samir from Redwood, i'll hand off to ava in a sec to run the SDK walkthrough. can you just quickly confirm roles on the call?
[00:12] Jared: yeah i'm jared cto at vela, with maya on backend and priya for security, ethan's front end.
[00:18] Maya: hello
[00:19] Priya: hi
[00:20] Ava: great, cool — thanks. objective here is to show the python and typescript quickstarts, auth patterns, and how you'd set up environments in the console for a pilot. any must-hit items?
[00:30] Jared: mainly auth and data residency — we need to make sure logs and payloads don't leak, and we want a preview of the cost model. also curious about a private deployment option.
[00:40] Samir: understood. we'll cover hosted first, then dedicated / private options. ava — hand off?
[00:45] Ava: yep, thanks. i'll share my screen — (screen share noise) — ok, starting with the python quickstart. so our sdk is pip install redwood-inference, basic usage looks like: 
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate("Summarize this text")
print(resp.text)

[01:20] Maya: quick q, how do we handle env separation? like staging keys vs prod?
[01:26] Ava: good point — we recommend using per-environment API keys with RBAC tied to the console. in hosted, you can create tokens scoped to routes. in private, you'd use your internal k8s secrets and KMS for key rotation.
[01:40] Priya: what about SSO? we generally want SAML for the console and service-level oauth for apps.
[01:46] Ava: we support SAML SSO for the console, SCIM provisioning, and we have an OAuth client flow for service accounts if you need short-lived tokens. for programmatic access most customers use api keys with enforced rotation via our console or their KMS.
[01:58] Ethan: is there a way to do typed responses in TS? we want to pipe model responses into our ui components.
[02:05] Ava: yep, our TS sdk has types out of the box. quick demo — (switches to TS file) npm i @redwood/inference; const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY }); const res = await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] }); console.log(res.choices[0].message.content);
[02:35] Jared: are there rate limits per key? how does throttling work if we burst?
[02:42] Samir: hosted has per-account and per-route rate limits you can configure; for predictable throughput we recommend Dedicated where you reserve capacity and avoid throttling. we also expose soft quotas and burst buckets.
[02:56] Maya: curious about cost, can you show the cost view in console?
[03:00] Ava: yeah — (navigates) in console -> billing -> token usage you get token-level breakdowns, per-route costs and per-model. you can also set cost alerts and usage thresholds.
[03:20] Priya: audit logs — we need immutable logs for compliance and ability to export to our SIEM.
[03:28] Ava: we provide audit logs export via S3/Cloud Storage, and you can configure log retention. for private deployments those logs stay inside your VPC and talk to your SIEM.
[03:40] Jared: can you walk through a sample quickstart for a pilot? like sample QPS, concurrency, how to pick the model.
[03:48] Ava: sure. first, share sample traffic — typical pilot we ask for: avg tokens per request, peak qps, and percent of chat vs single-turn generation. based on that we recommend model family (e.g., redwood-small/med/large or open variants), quantization profile, and batching settings. i'll attach a benchmark checklist.
[04:12] Maya: when you say quantization profile do you mean 4-bit/8-bit? what's supported?
[04:18] Ava: we support 8-bit, 4-bit dynamic for some families — depends on architecture. our optimize tool will recommend a quantization+batching combo per workload to hit target latency and cost. note: for very low-latency interactive ui we suggest lighter models or dedicated capacity.
[04:40] Ethan: any sdk gotchas for browser usage? we don't want to expose keys in client.
[04:45] Samir: yes, don't put keys in browser — route calls through your backend and use short-lived tokens or an edge proxy. we have examples in the quickstart showing a backend relay.
[04:58] Jared: could you show how to create scoped tokens in console?
[05:02] Ava: sure — (navigates) console -> project -> api keys -> new key. you can set scope (read/write, model routes), expiration, and attach to a route. the UI also shows last used and rotating.
[05:20] Priya: about encryption at rest — do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:24] Ava: hosted offers encryption with provider-managed keys; we offer CMKs (customer-managed keys) for enterprise tiers and private deployment supports using your HSM/KMS. i'll flag this for samir to send the security doc.
[05:40] Maya: can we get sample code for batching — like server side batcher?
[05:46] Ava: yep, we provide an example using our python sdk with an asyncio batcher: gather requests for up to N tokens or M ms and then call client.batch.generate([...]). i'll paste that snippet in the repo.
[06:05] Ethan: how does the streaming api look in ts? we want progressive rendering.
[06:10] Ava: our streaming supports server-sent events and websocket. TS snippet: const stream = client.stream.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages }); stream.on('data', chunk => renderChunk(chunk)); stream.on('end', () => finalize());
[06:30] Jared: we have an on prem constraint for some data. if we go private, what's the typical deployment footprint?
[06:36] Samir: for private on-prem we provide an installable package or helm chart, typical footprint depends on model sizes — a small pilot can run on a couple of A100s or equivalent; for production you'd size to your qps and model choices. dedicated reserved capacity is in between — fully managed but isolated GPUs.
[06:58] Priya: do you have SOC2 / ISO docs? customers ask.
[07:02] Ava: yes, we have a SOC2 report and ISO summary for enterprise customers. samir will send access to the compliance pack.
[07:12] Jared: what about latency SLOs?
[07:15] Samir: hosted SLOs vary by model class, but we have p95 targets documented. Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and uptime. we'll share perf decks.
[07:30] Maya: one more about SDKs — we do a lot of typed schema outputs. any support for function-calling or structured outputs?
[07:36] Ava: yes we support function/tool-calling and structured output parsers. ts sdk can infer types and we have server side validators. i'll link the function-calling quickstart.
[07:50] Ethan: is there an official starter repo?
[07:52] Ava: yes — github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts — with python, ts, server-relay, and benchmarks. samir will share the private starter that has a minimal CI config for pilot.
[08:05] Jared: ok good. let's move on to an integration demo — maybe walk through a tiny python app connecting and sending a request.
[08:12] Ava: absolutely. demo: terminal -> export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_XXXXX; python app.py (app code shown) — it calls client.generate with a prompt and returns text. note the sdk has retry/backoff built-in for transient 5xx from the infra.
[08:40] Maya: do you expose per-request metadata for tracing? we want to connect traces to our observability stack.
[08:46] Ava: yes you can attach request_id and parent_trace to the call; we surface traces in console and export to tracing backends via traces export.
[08:58] Priya: one sec — about retention policy for prompts — how long do you keep text by default?
[09:05] Samir: default retention is 30 days for hosted, configurable per-account; enterprise/private can set to zero retention. we'll include retention options in the security doc.
[09:18] Ethan: what about embargoed model weights or vendor lock? we use open models mainly.
[09:24] Ava: you can pick open variants from our model catalog; we also list provenance and license info. Optimize can help you pick a quantized variant that matches requirements.
[09:36] Jared: any known gotchas when migrating from openai APIs?
[09:40] Samir: mostly naming and response shape differences; we have mapping guides and an open-source shim that maps common OpenAI calls to redwood SDK calls. we'll share that link.
[09:54] Maya: do you offer rate limiting per route so we can protect downstream services?
[09:59] Ava: yes per-route throttles and per-user quotas supported. you can set them in policies and attach them to keys.
[10:10] Jared: ok we need to talk pilot metrics — what do you need from our side?
[10:15] Ava: sample traffic, target p95 latency, cost target, retention/security needs, and a list of anchor prompts for quality evals. we'll run an initial benchmark and tune batch/quant.
[10:30] Priya: security follow-up: can we do a vulnerability scan on your docker images before deploying private?
[10:36] Samir: yes we provide signed images and vulnerability scan reports. for private we can support your scanners in a staging run.
[10:45] Jared: timeline — we want a 4-week pilot to validate latency/cost and an internal stakeholder demo by mid-april. is that doable?
[10:53] Samir: yes typical pilot 2-6 weeks; we'll plan for kickoff week of 2026-03-29 and check-in weekly.
[11:05] Maya: ok can you repeat what you'll send after this call?
[11:07] Samir: sure — quickstart repo, benchmark checklist, security pack (SOC2 + CMK details), and a proposed pilot runbook.
[11:15] Ava: i'll also include sample batcher code, streaming examples, and a TS typed example for function calling.
[11:25] Priya: please include contact for compliance to loop in if we have questions.
[11:28] Samir: noted.
[11:30] Jared: anything else?
[11:32] Ethan: one UI question — any latency numbers for streaming first byte for chat models?
[11:36] Ava: for hosted chat we'd expect first byte ~120-250ms for smaller models under light load; dedicated lowers that and quantization can help. actuals depend on model and tokens. we'll include perf tables.
[11:55] Maya: that's helpful.
[12:00] Samir: ok let's wrap. next steps recap: samir sends docs + repo, ava sends benchmark scripts, priya to return security answers. pilot kickoff week of 3/29.
[12:18] Jared: thanks everyone.
[12:20] Priya: thanks
[12:22] Ava: thanks all
[12:24] Samir: bye

(End of recording)
